land.text: Shayzar (Shaizar) and its lands, the 1025 iqta

predecessors.note: 'Salih granted the Munqhidite chieftain, Muqallad ibn Nasr ibn Munqidh, the lands around Shayzar as an iqta' in 1025; 'the family entered the service of Salih ibn Mirdas, founder of the Aleppo-based Mirdasid dynasty' (Banu Munqidh page).

land.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

successors.note: 'seized by Nur al-Din to prevent its capture by the Crusaders' after the August 1157 earthquake (Banu Munqidh page); Nur al-Din 'incorporated the remains into his territory' (Shaizar page).

capitals.name: Kafartab
capitals.note: 'the Banu Munqidh instead used Kafartab as their headquarters'. The pages give no coordinates for Kafartab: the point is Shayzar's (35.2678 N, 36.5667 E, Shaizar page), the nearest fix they give, at confidence 1.

capitals.name: Shayzar
capitals.note: 'took over the fortress of Shayzar in 1081 and made it their headquarters for the remainder of their rule'; coordinates 35.2678 N 36.5667 E (Shaizar page).

rulers.name: Ali ibn Muqallad
rulers.title: emir
rulers.note: 'Under the reign of Emir Ali ibn Muqallad (r. 1059-1082), the Banu Munqidh reached their territorial peak'; the Shaizar page lists 'Izz ad-Dawla Sadid al-Mulk ibn Munqidh' for 1081-1082.

rulers.name: Nasr ibn Ali
rulers.note: 'Ali was succeeded by his son Nasr'; 'In 1098, Nasr died and the lordship of Shayzar passed to his brothers'.

rulers.name: Sultan ibn Ali
rulers.note: 'Under Emir Sultan ibn Ali (r. 1098-1154)'. In 1127 he put the emirate under Zengi's suzerainty; his brother Murshid, the deputy, died in 1136/37.

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn Sultan
rulers.note: 'the death of Emir Muhammad ibn Sultan (r. 1154-1157) and his family in the 1157 earthquake'.

correction.text: Shayzar (Shaizar) and its lands, the 1025 iqta

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Banu Munqidh). 1025: 'the lands around Shayzar as an iqta', with the town itself Byzantine and the family seated at Kafartab. The page gives no area: a 25 km disc at Shayzar (35.2678 N, 36.5667 E, Shaizar page) is drawn.

'Under the reign of Emir Ali ibn Muqallad (r. 1059-1082), the Banu Munqidh reached their territorial peak' with 'the emirate extending from the Mediterranean port of Latakia to Apamea' and 'Apamea and a few smaller places, in addition to Shayzar and Kafartab'. The page does not date the acquisitions inside the reign; they are placed at 1059.

region.text: Shayzar (Shaizar) and its lands, the 1025 iqta

ledger.note: 1025: 'Upon capturing Aleppo in 1025, Salih granted the Munqhidite chieftain, Muqallad ibn Nasr ibn Munqidh, the lands around Shayzar as an iqta'; infobox 'Founded: 1025'. 'The town of Shayzar itself was in Byzantine hands, however'; the family used Kafartab as headquarters. An iqta under Mirdasid overlordship, so the founding is the infobox's, not an independence.

ledger.counterpart: holders of Latakia, Apamea and Kafartab (the page names none)
ledger.note: Page silent on the year within the reign: 'Under the reign of Emir Ali ibn Muqallad (r. 1059-1082), the Banu Munqidh reached their territorial peak ... extending from the Mediterranean port of Latakia to Apamea'; placed at 1059, the start of the reign.

region.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

ledger.note: December 1081: Ali 'compelled its Byzantine rulers to surrender the fortress to Ali in December 1081' (Banu Munqidh page); 'It was lost to the Banu Munqidh in 1081 when Ali ibn Munqidh bought it from the bishop' (Shaizar page). The town lies inside the 25 km disc of the 1025 frame.

1086: 'The Seljuk conquest of Syria in 1085'; Nasr 'had to submit to the Seljuk Sultan Malik-Shah I' in 1086 (Shaizar page) and ceded 'Latakia, Apamea and Kafartab to the sultanate' (Banu Munqidh page). The page gives 1085 for the conquest and no year for the cession; the Shaizar page's 1086 is used.

ledger.counterpart: Aq Sunqur al-Hajib (Seljuk governor of Aleppo)
ledger.note: 1091: 'Aq Sunqur al-Hajib, the Seljuk ruler of Aleppo, returned the towns in 1091 after Nasr's appeal to him' (Banu Munqidh page). The Shaizar page adds that around 1088/89 Aqsunqur 'besieged the town and ravaged it'.

ledger.counterpart: Khalaf ibn Mula'ib (former lord of Homs)
ledger.note: 1096: 'in 1096 Apamea and Kafartab were lost to the family's Arab rival, Khalaf ibn Mula'ib'.

ledger.counterpart: holder of Latakia (the page names none)
ledger.note: Page silent: Latakia is not followed after its return in 1091; the page says only that the emirate was 'reduced ... to Shayzar and its environs'. Dropped with Apamea and Kafartab at confidence 1.

region.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

ledger.note: August 1157: the earthquake kills Emir Muhammad ibn Sultan and the family in the collapse of the Shayzar citadel; the principality 'was soon after seized by Nur al-Din to prevent its capture by the Crusaders'. Nur al-Din gave the town to Sabiq al-Din Uthman ibn al-Daya, whose family held it to 1233 (Banu Munqidh page).

region.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

ledger.note: 1157: infobox 'Dissolution: 1157', final ruler Muhammad ibn Sultan.

wars.name: Tancred and the Crusader coalition against Shayzar

zones.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

wars.outcome: Tancred 'attacked and plundered the Banu Munqidh's emirate in 1110' and then 'gathered a larger Crusader coalition including the rulers of Jerusalem and Tripoli'; 'the Crusader armies retreated in October 1111' (Banu Munqidh page; the Shaizar page: 'the battle of Shaizar of 1111').

wars.name: Byzantine siege of Shayzar

zones.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

wars.outcome: 'In April 1138, the Byzantine army led the siege of Shaizar'; 'Zengi soon arrived to relieve the fortress in May' (Shaizar page).

certainty.note: No page gives an area or frontier: the discs round Shayzar, Latakia, Apamea and Kafartab are approximations, and the page dates none of the peak acquisitions within Ali's reign (1059-1082).

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages opened (Banu Munqidh, Shaizar), within budget. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Dates: the infobox has 'Mirdasid Emirate (1025-1080); Seljuk Empire (1080-1127); Zengid Atabegate (1127-1157)' as its status line and 'Founded: 1025', 'Dissolution: 1157'. Salih ibn Mirdas's 1025 grant was an iqta of the lands round Shayzar, not independence; the family sat at Kafartab until it took Shayzar in December 1081. Suzerain-side vassal events (not recorded here): the Mirdasids to 1080 (mirdasid-dynasty has no Munqidh event), the Seljuks 1086, Zengi from 1127 ('Sultan put the Banu Munqidh under the suzerainty of the ascendant Muslim ruler of Mosul and Aleppo'); the zengid-dynasty dossier has no Shayzar event.
Territory: Shayzar and its lands, Kafartab, Apamea and Latakia at the peak under Ali ibn Muqallad; Kafartab is not in the gazetteer and the capital point is a bridge. The Banu al-Daya held Shayzar 'until 1233' after 1157 (the Shaizar page does not say this; the Banu Munqidh page does). The Assassins took the ruins of Shaizar after Ridwan's death in 1113 (Shaizar page, 'defeated by the Crusaders in 1158'); the Shaizar page also has Saladin taking 'the remnants' in 1174 and Baibars rebuilding the city in 1260 (not Munqidh events).
Mirrors: mirdasid-dynasty has no 1025 grant; great-seljuk-empire has no Latakia/Apamea/Kafartab events for 1086 and 1091; byzantine-empire has no 1081 Shayzar loss; principality-of-antioch and kingdom-of-jerusalem carry no Shayzar war (1110-1111); zengid-dynasty has no 1157 Shayzar gain.
Not settled: when within 1059-1082 Latakia and Apamea were gained; what happened to Latakia after 1091; the Hama/Homs borders of Khalaf ibn Mula'ib's land.
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Kafartab (place).
